mean: heard so often one knows it by heart
lit: the ear knows it so well that one can tell it in detail

story.text: Ouyang Xiu lost his father when he was a small child, and his mother told him what kind of man his father had been. In the memorial he later wrote for his parents, he records her saying that his father used certain words so often when teaching the younger members of the family that her ears had grown used to them, and so she could repeat them in detail.

use.how: Predicate or attribute: 这个故事大家都耳熟能详 / 耳熟能详的歌. Said of stories, songs, sayings or names heard again and again.

near.diff: 家喻户晓 says something is known in every household; 耳熟能详 says a person has heard it so often they could retell it.

cue: Your grandfather has told the same three war stories at every family dinner for years, and you could now tell them yourself.

ctx.s: 这首儿歌大家都{耳熟能详}。
ctx.en: Everyone knows this children's song by heart.

ctx.s: 《西游记》里的故事，中国孩子几乎都{耳熟能详}。
ctx.en: Nearly every Chinese child knows the stories of Journey to the West inside out.

ctx.s: 这句广告词天天在电视上播，连老人都{耳熟能详}了。
ctx.en: That advertising slogan is on TV every day; even the elderly can recite it now.

ctx.s: “你听过这句名言吗？”“当然，从小听到大，早就{耳熟能详}了。”
ctx.en: "Have you heard this famous saying?" "Of course; I've heard it all my life and know it by heart."

ctx.s: 他讲的都是些{耳熟能详}的道理，可真正做到的人并不多。
ctx.en: What he talks about are principles we've all heard countless times, yet few people actually live by them.

ctx.s: 奶奶常讲家乡的往事，我早已{耳熟能详}，连细节都说得出来。
ctx.en: Grandma often talks about the old days back home; I've heard it so often I can give you every detail.

bad.s: 我对他的长相{耳熟能详}。
bad.en: (meant: I know his face very well)
bad.why: The idiom is about things heard over and over, such as stories or songs, not about faces or things one has seen.

bad.s: 我{耳熟能详}这首歌。
bad.en: (meant: I know this song by heart)
bad.why: It does not take a direct object; put the thing first: 'this song, I know it by heart', or use 'dui ... er shu neng xiang'.

lit: a scorched head and a burnt forehead

story.text: A guest saw that a house had a straight chimney with firewood piled beside it and told the owner to build a bent chimney and move the wood, or there would be a fire. The owner ignored him. Soon the house caught fire and the neighbours put it out. To thank them the owner gave a feast, seating those with scorched heads and burnt foreheads in the places of honour, but he never invited the man who had warned him.

use.how: Usually after 得 or as a result: 忙得焦头烂额, 被……搞得焦头烂额. Describes someone worn down by a pile of troubles or urgent tasks.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is flustered fumbling in one hectic moment; 焦头烂额 is being battered by many troubles over days or weeks.

cue: This month your landlord sold the flat, your car broke down and your boss moved the deadline forward. How do you describe your state?

ctx.s: 这几天又是搬家又是加班，我忙得{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: These past few days I've been moving house and working overtime, and I'm completely swamped.

ctx.s: 孩子生病，工作又出了问题，她被弄得{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: Her child is ill and there's trouble at work too; she's completely frazzled.

ctx.s: 年底各种报表一起来，财务部的人个个{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: At year's end all the reports land at once, and everyone in finance is at their wits' end.

ctx.s: “你怎么瘦了这么多？”“公司的事搞得我{焦头烂额}，哪有时间吃饭。”
ctx.en: "Why have you lost so much weight?" "Things at the company have me so swamped I have no time to eat."

ctx.s: 新产品一上市就接到大量投诉，经理正{焦头烂额}地处理。
ctx.en: The new product drew a flood of complaints as soon as it launched, and the manager is scrambling to deal with them.

ctx.s: 与其等问题堆起来弄得{焦头烂额}，不如现在就早做准备。
ctx.en: Rather than wait until the problems pile up and overwhelm you, it's better to prepare now.

bad.s: 他工作{焦头烂额}，真是个好员工。
bad.en: (meant: he works very hard; he's a great employee)
bad.why: It describes being overwhelmed and harried by trouble, not diligence, so it is not praise for hard work.

bad.s: 他做饭的时候不小心{焦头烂额}了。
bad.en: (meant: he burned himself while cooking)
bad.why: In modern use it is only figurative, about being swamped by problems; it is never used for real burns.

mean: without a single idea of how to deal with it
lit: hands as if tied, and not one plan

use.how: Predicate, often 对……束手无策 or 一时束手无策. Said of someone facing a problem who wants to act but cannot think of any way.

near.diff: 无能为力 says something is beyond one's power, often when declining to help; 束手无策 says one has no idea at all what to do.

cue: Your car dies on a dark country road, you know nothing about engines, and your phone has no signal.

ctx.s: 电脑突然死机了，我完全{束手无策}。
ctx.en: My computer suddenly froze and I had no idea what to do.

ctx.s: 面对这种罕见的病，年轻医生一时{束手无策}，只好去请教老专家。
ctx.en: Faced with such a rare disease, the young doctor had no idea what to do and had to go and ask a senior specialist.

ctx.s: 孩子哭个不停，新手爸爸{束手无策}地站在一旁。
ctx.en: The baby wouldn't stop crying, and the new father stood beside it, helpless and clueless.

ctx.s: “水管漏水了，怎么办？”“我也{束手无策}，赶快叫师傅吧。”
ctx.en: "The pipe's leaking, what do we do?" "I haven't a clue either; call a plumber, quick."

ctx.s: 洪水来得太快，村民们一时{束手无策}。
ctx.en: The flood came so fast that for a moment the villagers didn't know what to do.

ctx.s: 遇到困难不能{束手无策}，先冷静下来想想办法。
ctx.en: When you hit trouble you can't just stand there helpless; calm down first and think of a way.

bad.s: 他不想帮忙，就{束手无策}地站在旁边看。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't want to help, so he just stood by and watched)
bad.why: It means wanting to act but having no way to; standing by on purpose is a different idea, expressed by 'xiu shou pang guan'.

bad.s: 我实在{束手无策}他。
bad.en: (meant: I can't do anything about him)
bad.why: It takes no object; the pattern is 'dui ta shu shou wu ce', 'about him I am at a loss'.

lit: the heart at peace, because reason is on one's side

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 心安理得地收下. Said of feeling no guilt; often critical, about someone untroubled by what should trouble them.

near.diff: 问心无愧 declares that one has done nothing wrong; 心安理得 is the easy, guilt-free feeling, often said ironically of someone who should feel bad.

cue: Your flatmate eats your food every day without asking and doesn't feel the slightest bit bad about it.

ctx.s: 这钱是我自己辛苦挣的，花得{心安理得}。
ctx.en: I earned this money through my own hard work, so I spend it with a clear conscience.

ctx.s: 他把同事的功劳算在自己头上，还一副{心安理得}的样子。
ctx.en: He took credit for his colleague's work and looks perfectly at ease about it.

ctx.s: 她每天让父母做饭洗衣，自己{心安理得}地玩手机。
ctx.en: Every day she lets her parents cook and do the laundry while she plays on her phone without a second thought.

ctx.s: 这么贵重的礼物，我怎么能{心安理得}地收下？
ctx.en: How could I accept such an expensive gift with an easy conscience?

ctx.s: 把借的钱全部还清以后，他才{心安理得}地过了个年。
ctx.en: Only after paying back all the money he'd borrowed could he enjoy the New Year with his mind at ease.

ctx.s: 有些人占了公家的便宜，不但不脸红，反而{心安理得}。
ctx.en: Some people help themselves to public property and, far from blushing, feel entirely entitled.

bad.s: 考试结束了，我终于{心安理得}了。
bad.en: (meant: the exam is over and I'm finally relieved)
bad.why: It is about feeling morally justified, not about relief after stress; for relief say 'song le yi kou qi'.

bad.s: 这个房间很安静，让人{心安理得}。
bad.en: (meant: this room is quiet and makes you feel calm)
bad.why: It concerns one's conscience about what one has done, not calm caused by a peaceful place.

lit: hearts shine on each other, but nothing is declared

use.how: Adverbial with 地 or attribute with 的: 心照不宣地笑了, 心照不宣的秘密. Said of two or more people who all know something but none says it.

near.diff: 心领神会 is grasping someone's hint at once; 心照不宣 stresses that everyone knows and all keep quiet about it.

cue: The boss says 'let's revisit this later', and everyone at the table knows it means no; they just nod, and nobody says it aloud.

ctx.s: 花瓶是谁打碎的，兄妹俩{心照不宣}，谁也不说破。
ctx.en: Brother and sister both knew who had broken the vase, but neither said a word about it.

ctx.s: 他们俩在谈恋爱，这是办公室里{心照不宣}的秘密。
ctx.en: That the two of them are dating is the office's open secret that nobody mentions.

ctx.s: 老板说“再考虑考虑”，大家都{心照不宣}：这事没戏了。
ctx.en: The boss said "let's think about it more", and everyone silently understood: it's dead.

ctx.s: “这件事要不要跟他说清楚？”“不用了，彼此{心照不宣}就好。”
ctx.en: "Should we spell it out to him?" "No need; it's better if we both just understand without saying."

ctx.s: 比赛快结束时，两支球队{心照不宣}地放慢了节奏。
ctx.en: Near the end of the match, both teams slowed the pace by tacit agreement.

ctx.s: 他们从不提那次吵架，像是有个{心照不宣}的约定。
ctx.en: They never mention that quarrel, as if they had an unspoken pact.

bad.s: 我{心照不宣}地把真相告诉了他。
bad.en: (meant: I quietly told him the truth)
bad.why: It means the matter is understood without being said, so it cannot describe actually telling someone.

bad.s: 他{心照不宣}，可我什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: he kept it to himself, and I knew nothing)
bad.why: The understanding must be shared by both sides; for one person keeping a secret say 'bao mi' or 'bu ken shuo'.

lit: the heart anxious as if it were on fire

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地. Said of someone burning with worry when something bad may be happening or time is running out.

near.diff: 坐立不安 shows restlessness and can be mild nerves; 心急如焚 is burning, urgent worry, as when someone may be in danger.

cue: Your child hasn't come home from school, it's getting dark, and nobody answers the phone.

ctx.s: 孩子发高烧不退，妈妈{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: The child's high fever won't come down, and the mother is frantic.

ctx.s: 女儿到半夜还没回家，电话也打不通，我{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: My daughter still wasn't home at midnight and her phone was unreachable; I was beside myself with worry.

ctx.s: 父亲病重，他却被困在机场，{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: His father was gravely ill, yet he was stuck at the airport, frantic.

ctx.s: “医生，我丈夫怎么样了？”她{心急如焚}地问。
ctx.en: "Doctor, how is my husband?" she asked desperately.

ctx.s: 眼看截止时间就要到了，文件还没传上去，小王{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: The deadline was nearly upon him and the file still hadn't uploaded; Xiao Wang was frantic.

ctx.s: 得知家乡发生地震，在外地工作的人们{心急如焚}，纷纷打电话回家。
ctx.en: Hearing of the earthquake back home, people working elsewhere were desperate with worry and rushed to phone their families.

bad.s: 他是个{心急如焚}的人，做什么都很快。
bad.en: (meant: he's an impatient person who does everything fast)
bad.why: It is a passing state of intense worry, not a personality trait; an impatient person is 'ji xing zi'.

bad.s: 今天天气太热了，我{心急如焚}。
bad.en: (meant: it's so hot today, I'm burning up)
bad.why: The fire is only an image for worry; it says nothing about feeling physically hot.

lit: the heart opened wide, the spirit delighted

story.text: Fan Zhongyan wrote an essay for the rebuilt Yueyang Tower overlooking Dongting Lake. He describes climbing the tower on a clear spring day, with calm water, sunlight and endless views, and says that a person standing there feels the heart open wide and the spirit at ease, forgetting both honour and disgrace.

use.how: Predicate, often in 让人/令人心旷神怡. Said of the calm, refreshed feeling given by wide views, fresh air or beautiful surroundings.

near.diff: 心满意足 is the satisfaction of getting what one wanted; 心旷神怡 is the open, refreshed feeling a place or view gives.

cue: After weeks in a cramped office, you reach a mountain top and see sea and sky stretching out in front of you in a cool breeze.

ctx.s: 站在山顶往下看，真让人{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: Looking down from the mountain top is truly refreshing to the soul.

ctx.s: 海风迎面吹来，我感到{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: The sea breeze blew in my face and I felt wonderfully refreshed.

ctx.s: 雨后的公园空气清新，散步的人都觉得{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: After the rain the park air is fresh, and everyone out walking feels relaxed and uplifted.

ctx.s: “草原上的风景怎么样？”“蓝天白云，一望无际，叫人{心旷神怡}！”
ctx.en: "What's the scenery like on the grasslands?" "Blue sky, white clouds, as far as the eye can see; it lifts your spirits!"

ctx.s: 推开窗，湖光山色尽收眼底，他顿时{心旷神怡}，疲劳全消。
ctx.en: He opened the window to the whole view of lake and hills, and at once felt refreshed, his tiredness gone.

ctx.s: 这篇游记把江南写得很美，读来令人{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: This travel essay paints the south so beautifully that reading it is refreshing in itself.

bad.s: 听到考试通过的消息，我{心旷神怡}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing I'd passed the exam, I was overjoyed)
bad.why: It is the calm, open feeling given by scenery or surroundings, not excitement at good news.

bad.s: 我们{心旷神怡}了这里的风景。
bad.en: (meant: we enjoyed the scenery here)
bad.why: It takes no object; say the scenery 'rang ren xin kuang shen yi', makes people feel refreshed.

mean: engraved on one's heart, never forgotten
lit: carved into the bone, engraved on the heart

use.how: Mostly attribute: 刻骨铭心的爱情 / 教训 / 经历; also predicate. Said of deep love, pain, gratitude or lessons that mark one for life.

near.diff: 记忆犹新 says a memory is still vivid; 刻骨铭心 says an experience left a deep emotional mark that will last a lifetime.

cue: Fifty years on, your grandmother still cannot speak of the night she said goodbye to her first love without tears.

ctx.s: 那是一段{刻骨铭心}的爱情。
ctx.en: It was a love she would never forget.

ctx.s: 第一次创业失败，给了他一个{刻骨铭心}的教训。
ctx.en: His first failed business taught him a lesson he'll carry for life.

ctx.s: 战争的经历对爷爷来说{刻骨铭心}，他一辈子都忘不了。
ctx.en: For Grandpa the war was seared into him; he never forgot it his whole life.

ctx.s: “你还记得高考那天吗？”“当然，那种紧张的感觉真是{刻骨铭心}。”
ctx.en: "Do you remember the day of the college entrance exam?" "Of course; that tension is still burned into me."

ctx.s: 在异国他乡生病的那个冬天，是我一生中最{刻骨铭心}的日子。
ctx.en: That winter I fell ill far from home in a foreign country was the most unforgettable time of my life.

ctx.s: 老师在我最困难时给我的帮助，我至今{刻骨铭心}。
ctx.en: The help my teacher gave me when I was at my lowest is still engraved on my heart.

bad.s: 昨天的午饭很好吃，真是{刻骨铭心}。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday's lunch was delicious and memorable)
bad.why: It is far too heavy for an ordinary pleasant thing; it is reserved for experiences of deep love, pain or gratitude.

bad.s: 我把这些单词背得{刻骨铭心}。
bad.en: (meant: I've memorised these words thoroughly)
bad.why: It is about emotional experiences that mark a person, not rote memorising; say 'bei de hen shu'.

lit: something troubling held in one's breast and never let go

use.how: Predicate, often 对……耿耿于怀 or 一直耿耿于怀. Said of a slight, an injustice or a defeat that someone cannot let go of.

near.diff: 念念不忘 is keeping something constantly in mind, often fondly; 耿耿于怀 is only for a grievance or setback that still rankles.

cue: Three years ago a friend forgot your birthday party, and you still bring it up with a sour face.

ctx.s: 别再为那点小事{耿耿于怀}了。
ctx.en: Stop dwelling on such a small thing.

ctx.s: 他至今还对那次被冤枉{耿耿于怀}。
ctx.en: He still can't get over being wrongly accused that time.

ctx.s: 比赛只输了一分，队员们好几天都{耿耿于怀}。
ctx.en: They lost by a single point, and the players were still brooding over it days later.

ctx.s: “你还在生我的气吗？”“说实话，你那天的话我一直{耿耿于怀}。”
ctx.en: "Are you still angry with me?" "Honestly, what you said that day still rankles."

ctx.s: 没被提拔这件事，她一直{耿耿于怀}，工作也没了热情。
ctx.en: She has never got over being passed for promotion, and has lost all enthusiasm for her work.

ctx.s: 生活中不如意的事很多，总是{耿耿于怀}只会让自己更累。
ctx.en: Life is full of disappointments; nursing every one of them only wears you out.

bad.s: 我一直对奶奶做的饺子{耿耿于怀}。
bad.en: (meant: I've never forgotten Grandma's dumplings)
bad.why: It is only for grievances and setbacks that still rankle, never for fond memories; use 'nian nian bu wang' instead.

bad.s: 他一直{耿耿于怀}我。
bad.en: (meant: he holds a grudge against me)
bad.why: It takes no direct object; the pattern is 'ta dui wo geng geng yu huai'.

mean: unable to stop thinking about something
lit: thinking of it thought after thought, never forgetting

use.how: Predicate, often 对……念念不忘, or attribute: 念念不忘的人. Said of a person, place, taste or goal one keeps returning to in one's mind.

near.diff: 耿耿于怀 is brooding over a grievance; 念念不忘 is keeping something in mind, usually something one misses or longs for.

cue: Years after a trip to Chengdu, you still talk about one little noodle shop there and keep saying you must go back.

ctx.s: 他对那家小店的牛肉面{念念不忘}。
ctx.en: He still can't stop thinking about the beef noodles at that little shop.

ctx.s: 回国好多年了，她还{念念不忘}在法国留学的日子。
ctx.en: She's been back home for years, yet she still thinks fondly of her student days in France.

ctx.s: 爷爷最{念念不忘}的，是老家门前那棵大槐树。
ctx.en: What Grandpa misses most is the big locust tree in front of his old home.

ctx.s: “你怎么又提起她了？”“没办法，我就是对她{念念不忘}。”
ctx.en: "Why are you bringing her up again?" "I can't help it; I just can't get her out of my mind."

ctx.s: 这位老科学家到了晚年，仍{念念不忘}那项没完成的研究。
ctx.en: Even in old age, the scientist never stopped thinking about his unfinished research.

ctx.s: 一次旅行让人{念念不忘}，往往不是因为风景，而是因为同行的人。
ctx.en: What makes a trip unforgettable is often not the scenery but the people you went with.

bad.s: 我每天出门都{念念不忘}带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: I always remember to take my keys when I go out)
bad.why: It means dwelling on something one longs for or cannot let go of, not remembering to do a routine task; just say 'ji de'.

bad.s: 他是个{念念不忘}的人，什么都记得。
bad.en: (meant: he has a great memory and remembers everything)
bad.why: It describes being preoccupied with one particular thing, not a good memory in general; say 'ji xing hao'.
